questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

Kiara was born in India but she went to ______ university in ______ United Kingdom.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**a; the**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The article "**a**" is used before the word "university" because "university" starts with a consonant sound.
 
• The article "**the**" is used before "United Kingdom" because it is a specific name of a country that includes the word "United."
 
• **Options 1, 2**, and **3** are grammatically incorrect in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"Kiara was born in India but she went to **a**__ university in __**the**__ United Kingdom."*

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four parts. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error.

Jack probably/ strained his back/ as the box was/ too heavier.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect comparative adjective "**heavier**" following the adverb "**too**."
 
• When using the word "too," the correct form should be "**too heavy**," not "too heavier."
 
• Comparative adjectives like** "heavier"** are used to compare two things, whereas **"too"** implies an excessive degree.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 3** of the sentence.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Jack probably strained his back as the box was **too heavy**."*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

As technology evolves, consumers increasingly _______________ products with enhanced features and greater efficiency.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**demand**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The context tells us that with technological advancement, customers are progressively seeking products offering improved features and higher efficiency.
 
• The verb "**demand**" is the **base form of the verb**, which is appropriate here because the sentence describes a general trend or habit.
 
• **"Demand"** is **plural **here (referring to consumers), so the verb form is **"demand."** The plural noun **"consumers"** correctly aligns with the plural verb **"demand,"** making it grammatically accurate.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"As technology evolves, consumers increasingly **demand**__ products with enhanced features and greater efficiency."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "might demand"** indicates a possibility rather than a trend, making it less suitable for this sentence.
 
• **Option 3: "has demanded"** suggests a completed action, which does not fit the ongoing nature of the trend described.
 
• **Option 4: "were demanding"** is in the past continuous tense, which does not match the context of an evolving trend.
